title: Chris Rock criticizes “wokeness” and defends forgiveness
seoTitle: Chris Rock criticizes 'wokeness' and defends forgiveness
subtitle: Comedian links cancel culture to the Old Testament
excerpt: In an interview, Chris Rock warns that 'wokeness' creates a less forgiving world, comparing it to the Old Testament and emphasizing the importance of forgiveness.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In an interview with The New York Times' program The Interview, Chris Rock stated that “wokeness” has created a less forgiving environment, comparing the current situation to the Old Testament. The comedian used the theme to discuss forgiveness, a central element of his new film Misty Green.

What Rock Understands by “Wokeness”

Rock defined “wokeness” as a movement that, while important for giving a voice to marginalized groups, can become rigid when institutionalized. He praised the original intention of amplifying these voices but warned that institutionalization leads to a lack of forgiveness.

Comparison to the Old Testament

The comedian explained that, in his view, we live “in the Old Testament,” where “there is no forgiveness.” He emphasized that the Old Testament “didn't work” and needed a “remix” called the New Testament, reinforcing his Christian belief in God's capacity to forgive.

Forgiveness as the Theme of Misty Green

In the interview, Rock described forgiveness as the guiding thread of Misty Green, a film he wrote and directed. The plot follows a declining actress attempting to return to Hollywood, facing an environment he calls “merciless.”

Friendship and the Limits of Cancellation

Rock mentioned having a friend “who may have been canceled” and stated that, for him, friendship should not depend on good times. He asserted that “if you're only friends when the person is doing well, you're not friends.” The comedian emphasized that it's possible to reprimand abusive behaviors without ceasing to forgive.

Analogy with Witch Hunts

To illustrate the danger of institutionalizing a movement, Rock drew an analogy with the Salem witch hunts, saying that by creating a “witch office,” needs arise to justify salaries and pensions, which leads to lies and injustices.

Interview Conclusion

Despite the criticisms, Rock acknowledged that the post-2020 period brought positive impacts by giving a voice to those who were previously silenced. He concluded by stating that he is happy for everything that happened, as it allowed him to hear voices he might not have heard otherwise.

With information from TheWrap.
